title: Poland's Underground Salt Cathedral ⛏️
hook_sentence: Near Kraków in southern Poland, the mine's rock salt naturally displays various shades of grey, resembling unpolished granite rather than white crystalline salt.
narration_script: Near Kraków in southern Poland, the mine's rock salt naturally displays various shades of grey, resembling unpolished granite rather than white crystalline salt. Engineering surveys and heritage records place the total extent of underground galleries between 287 and 300 kilometers. By one estimate, underground miners carved four chapels and dozens of statues directly out of the native rock salt. Wieliczka was designated as one of the original UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1978. Artificial ventilation introduced in the late nineteenth century brought humidity into the mine, threatening severe damage to the carved salt sculptures. Today, the subterranean chapels feature chandeliers carved out of natural rock salt.
closing_sentence: Today, the subterranean chapels feature chandeliers carved out of natural rock salt.
caption:
Centuries of subterranean carving created a massive sanctuary hidden beneath Poland. ⛏️

The Wieliczka Salt Mine is located in the town of Wieliczka, near Kraków in southern Poland. By one estimate, the mine excavations descend to a maximum depth of 327 meters below the surface, while engineering surveys and heritage records place the total extent of underground galleries between 287 and 300 kilometers.
